notes:
Summary: Obsidian runs high-frequency personalization and reranking at the edge of user sessions. They need predictable throughput and billing for committed GPU capacity. Current interest: Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane.

Workload details / targets:
- Primary workloads: real-time personalization (low-latency chat-like inference for recommendations), reranking for ad placements, embedding generation for similarity joins.
- p95 latency target: 60-120ms (model-dependent). P50 should be <30ms for quick serves.
- Throughput requirement: sustained 1.2M tokens/day (peak windows 3x), simultaneous QPS target 1,200 RPS at 16-token avg per request.
- Availability / SLA: 99.9% regional uptime target, 4-hour P1 response, scheduled maintenance windows limited to 02:00-04:00 local time. Requesting failover policy across regions and capacity tiers.

Cost modeling discussion (notes from pricing workshop):
- Tested commit tiers: Small (4 GPUs reserved), Medium (16 GPUs), Large (48 GPUs).
- Baseline assumptions: 12-hour effective GPU usage per day (50% utilization) vs optimized scenario 18-hour effective (75% utilization) when using batching + KV caching.
- Unit economics examples presented in deck v2: at 75% utilization and intelligent batching, estimated infra-only cost ~ $0.00035 per token for their LLM mix (mixed 7B and 13B variants, quantized FF). At 50% util cost increases to ~$0.0009/token.
- Break-even utilization: ~62% for the Medium tier given committed discount assumptions.
- Burst policy: pay-as-you-go burst pool for sudden spikes recommended; modeled as 20% incremental marginal cost on peak tokens.
- Reserved commit tradeoffs: larger commits reduce per-token infra cost but increase risk if traffic seasonal. Suggested grace: quarterly true-up and 10% flex burst capacity.

SLA & negotiation points:
- Penalties: Obsidian asked for credits tied to p99 latency breaches and regional downtime; proposing credits up to 10% of monthly fee for sustained SLA misses.
- Retry/fallback: need automatic fallback to smaller model variants in the Dedicated fleet or routed to Redwood-hosted for degraded performance scenarios.
- Data controls: all inference logs must be configurable retention and routed through customer KMS; audit logs required for last 180 days.

Open technical questions / action items from SE workshop:
- Provide detailed token-level cost calc for mixed-model serving (how cost splits between 7B/13B variants).
- Validate expected P50/P95 latency numbers on 16-GPU Medium cluster with their batching profile (avg seq len distribution attached in drive).
- Clarify model pinning + canary rollout semantics for private control plane.

Quotes / paraphrases from call:
- "We need cost certainty for FY27 planning — CAPEX lookahead for reserved GPUs must be defensible."
- "If the SLA is tight and penalties meaningful, we need a burnout plan to shift low-priority traffic off the dedicated pool."

Next practical steps:
- Jordan to deliver 3-tier revised proposal (with medium and large variants) and cost sensitivity table by 3/17.
- Legal to circulate redlines; SE to prepare P95 latency benchmark report (target delivery 3/18).
- Procurement to confirm internal budget window by 3/25.
